externalFinding: The adopted 2026–2027 regulations (26 May 2026), English Philosophy track, supply a coherent annual curriculum of 180 EC: ten compulsory 6 EC first-year units, eight compulsory and two selected 6 EC second-year units, and 30 EC open study plus two selected 6 EC philosophy electives, Bachelor Seminar III (6 EC) and an individual philosophy thesis (12 EC). The restricted choices are Theoretical Philosophy: Capita Selecta and World Philosophies I in Year 2, then History of Philosophy: Capita Selecta and Issues in Contemporary Ethics in Year 3. Each is taken once. One World Philosophies I/II unit is required across Years 2–3; the selected I meets it. The 2026–2027 annual plan is the comparator snapshot, not a guarantee of future optional-course topics. The thesis requires the entire first year and 48 EC from Year 2; all are completed before the final-year thesis in this pathway. The individual thesis formulates a philosophical question, independently selects literature and develops an argument under supervision; two readers assess it. Bachelor Seminar III trains its proposal, argument, literature search, chapter writing and peer feedback. Zero-credit Philosophical Encounters I and II and the English language test remain separate obligations. The diagnostic test or completed refresher gates the Skills: Academic English grade; BSA requires 42 first-year EC and the language-test quality condition. Annual Political Philosophy includes a Broader Mind certificate that validates its grade, within its 6 EC. Prior examination-board consent is normally needed for open study; individual electives include at least 12 EC at level 300. Eligible University minors and listed minors are exempt from prior consent, but Philosophy and Practical Philosophy minors are excluded for Philosophy students and compulsory overlap must be replaced with permission. Tutorials normally require 80% attendance; course requirements also apply, including compulsory argumentation/text seminars, all Logic quizzes and 75% Logic lecture attendance, and at most one missed Text Course II meeting. Honours is additional. English-named Philosophy and ENG registry provenance select the English track before UCR fit; Dutch Filosofie PLUS religion/theology or governance variants are separate and not merged into it. The current Dutch recruitment page simplifies its basic-track structure; the adopted English track annual plan controls this comparator.

comparability: Retain two qualified philosophical responses, with philosophy as the taught object and argument as its method, rather than replacing philosophy with generic cultural meaning. Six dedicated philosophy courses45EC per option (five PHIL plus Political Philosophy), Human Rights law/philosophy and ethical persuasion establish substantive depth and progression; logical reasoning and contexts support it. This is not a matching quota or degree equivalence. Seven-course52.5EC substitutions produce a real environmental/public-decisions direction. A third theoretical option repeats the same philosophical resources; Dutch PLUS religion/theology has neither selected-route status nor a sustained UCR disciplinary sequence. Stop at two.
